Mutations in MMADHC disrupt cobalamin (B12) metabolism. This leads to decreased conversion of methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA and impaired homocysteine remethylation. partners.diseaseBName: methylmalonic aciduria and homocystinuria type cblC
partners.mechanism_chain: MMADHC (HGNC:7409) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial cobalamin metabolism; MMACHC (HGNC:7407) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial cobalamin metabolism; Mitochondrial cobalamin metabolism —DECREASES→ Methylmalonyl-CoA (CHEBI:30796); Mitochondrial cobalamin metabolism —DECREASES→ Homocysteine (CHEBI:17606); Methylmalonyl-CoA (CHEBI:30796) —LEADS_TO→ Methylmalonic aciduria (HP:0001881); Homocysteine (CHEBI:17606) —LEADS_TO→ Homocystinuria (HP:0002138); PRDX1 (HGNC:9395) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial cobalamin metabolism. Mutations in MMADHC (cblD) and MMACHC (cblC) lead to defects in the mitochondrial cobalamin metabolism pathway. This disruption impairs the activity of enzymes that utilize adenosylcobalamin and methylcobalamin, leading to the accumulation of methylmalonyl-CoA and homocysteine, and consequently to methylmalonic aciduria and homocystinuria. PRDX1 is also implicated in cobalamin homeostasis, and its dysfunction can contribute to similar metabolic derangements.

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of MMADHC in both conditions allows for the development of unified therapeutic strategies targeting cobalamin metabolism or downstream metabolic consequences, potentially benefiting patients with either diagnosis.
